title: Casein preview-ui-walk manifest
description: App-owned contract for a UI smoke walk (.casein/preview-walk.json). Casein ships drivers + this schema; product repos own instances. Browser baseline: path/lands_on/budget/console/network/screenshot. Runtime (Tidewave): logs, project_eval probes, SELECT-only SQL, LiveView assign keys. Optional pages[].steps for assertions and (gated) interactions. Drivers skip runtime when Tidewave is unavailable and MUST mark that skip explicitly.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema (or a copy) for editor validation.

version.description: Schema version. Omit or set 1 for pages[]-only manifests. Set 2 when the manifest declares actions[] and/or the logins{} registry. v1 manifests remain valid unchanged.

pages.description: Screens to visit in order. Derive from the app router, not guesses.

logins.description: v2 account registry: login key → login definition. actions[].login selects one by key; the driver opens ONE browser context per key and logs in once per group (login-batching). Keys only ever name an account — secrets still resolve from params_from_env, never from this file. Omit to keep the single top-level login block.

actions.description: v2 unit of work: one user-observable action (usually one UAT issue) made of ordered phases that share a browser context, a carried-state bag and a single folded verdict. This is the only way to express a multi-navigation check such as edit → save → REOPEN → assert persisted, which pages[] cannot represent (each pages[] entry is an independent verdict). A v1 pages[] entry normalizes to a one-phase action internally.

prefix.description: Names records this walk creates, as {{fixture.prefix}} / {{fixture.run}} / {{fixture.tag}} in step text and runtime SQL. With no app-side audit trail this convention is the ONLY attribution available: it marks what the run CREATED (never what it edited), which on a shared dataset is the difference between finding the fixtures a failed cleanup left behind and never knowing they exist.

sweep_sql.description: SELECT-only, run once at the end of the walk, normally counting rows still matching {{fixture.tag}}. A non-zero result is reported loudly and recorded: cleanup is best-effort, so the last question worth answering is what this run left behind.

fixtures.description: Fixture identity and orphan sweep for records the walk creates.

prereq_policy.description: How unmet action prerequisites are handled. "check" (default, and the only mode implemented): an unmet predicate BLOCKS the action — correct for shared datasets, where the walk must never manufacture the state it is about to test. "seed" is reserved for isolated/disposable targets where the driver may create the missing fixture and re-check; declaring it now means adopting an isolated target later costs an executor, never a manifest rewrite.

strict_errors.description: When true, any raw console/network error fails the page (disables CSP noise filter).

noise_patterns.description: Extra case-insensitive regex sources treated as noise (merged with driver defaults).

workspace.description: OPTIONAL host hint: Casein agent-mcp env dir name (~/.casein/agent-mcp/<workspace>/env.sh). Prefer resolving workspace from launch env; product manifests should omit this when possible.

app_surface.description: OPTIONAL host hint for preview MCP walk.py (preview_surfaces name). Not used by playwright_walk.mjs.

_driver.description: Human annotation for which driver to prefer; ignored by drivers (login.kind/type selects the path).

viewports.description: Named viewports every page is walked at. Omit for the driver default (single viewport) — v1 behaviour.

require_evidence.description: Collectors that MUST produce evidence. A page whose required collector yields nothing is BLOCKED (not PASS, not FAILED) and the run fails closed. Omit for v1 behaviour: nothing is required. "prereq" routes action prerequisites through this same guard: a predicate that could not be EVALUATED (Tidewave down, SQL rejected) is missing evidence and BLOCKS — it must never inherit runtime's skipped: tidewave_unavailable degradation, which would delete the gate exactly when the environment is unhealthy.

source_identity.description: The EXPLICITLY accepted source identity whose baselines this walk compares against (e.g. a git sha or release label recorded at accept time). Part of the stable baseline key: baselines accepted under a different identity are never compared. Required whenever require_evidence includes visual_baseline.

store.description: Artifact-project name of the durable baseline store. Defaults to visual-baselines-<report.name>. Baselines always live in the Casein Artifact store (git-committed artifact worktree), never a local cache.

viewport.description: Named viewport recorded in the baseline key. Defaults to the first declared top-level viewport name, else "default".

visual_baseline.description: Visual-baseline comparison config (batch 3b). Comparison is compare-only during a walk: baselines are created/updated exclusively by the explicit visual_baseline.mjs accept action. Width, height and DPR must match the baseline exactly; changed pixels beyond 0.1% fail the page.

kind.description: Preferred product-facing auth model. Skill maps: redirect_cookie → playwright_walk.mjs; session → walk.py session inject; click → UI login; none → public pages.

type.description: Legacy driver field. cookie ≡ redirect_cookie; session_inject ≡ session. Prefer kind; drivers accept either.

params.description: Query/body params for the login route. Avoid hardcoding operator identity long-term; prefer env overrides at run time.

params_from_env.description: Env var names whose values are merged into login.params at run time (e.g. WALK_LOGIN_EMAIL).

lands_on.description: Expected post-login path prefix. Bounce to /login must fail the walk.

steps.description: Login prelude steps for kind:"click" (fill/click/assert). This is the shape the driver actually executes; the legacy `form` object is NOT read by the driver.

form.description: DEPRECATED and INERT: the driver never reads this. Use `steps`. Retained only so pre-existing v1 manifests validate; migrate them.

budget_ms.description: Wall-clock budget for the whole login prelude. Read by the driver (login.budget_ms); the post-login landing mount is usually the slowest hop in a walk.

site.description: Registry annotation: the tenant/site this account operates on. Surfaced in the report so a reader can tell WHICH dataset an action ran against.

unit_system.description: Registry annotation: the account's display unit system. A mismatch between two accounts compared against each other is a SETUP error, not a finding.

use_cases.description: Registry annotation: what this account can exercise (e.g. "VFD mixer", "fixed loads"). Human selection aid for choosing actions[].login; never read as a capability assertion — assert capability with a prereq predicate instead.

allOf.description: path/lands_on are required for every login kind EXCEPT "none" (public walks have no login route to assert).

evidence_key.description: The single source of truth for evidence keys. Walk-, action- and phase-level require_evidence all reference this; three inline copies would drift. NOTE on "audit_actor": no generic collector exists, because attribution needs an app-side audit trail with an actor column and the target app has none. Requiring it BLOCKS at preflight (exit 2) rather than mid-walk — loud and early, not a false pass. Until such a trail exists, a mutation on a SHARED dataset cannot be attributed to this walk: db_before_after can prove something changed, never that it was us.

name.description: Stable label. Groups the report, keys runtime.per_page, and is the unit written back to a tracker.

issue.description: Tracker issue this action verifies. One action ↔ one issue.

url.description: Canonical issue URL, for the report and any write-back adapter.

contract_hash.description: Hash of the issue's authored steps at the time this action was written. A mismatch means the human contract moved and the automation may no longer be testing what the issue says — surfaced, never auto-resolved. This is why issue Steps must not be edited cosmetically.

uat.description: Link to the human-authored contract. The issue owns WHAT should happen; this manifest owns HOW to drive it and what proves it.

login.description: Key into logins{}. Omit to use the single top-level login block. The driver groups actions by resolved login and logs in once per group.

prereq.description: Preconditions evaluated after session establishment and before phase 1 — 'is this action testable on this dataset right now?'. Unmet under prereq_policy:"check" BLOCKS the action (never FAILED: nothing was proved). Re-evaluated after ANY action failure; if a predicate held before and does not hold after, the verdict is reclassified BLOCKED/precondition_lost rather than charging the app for a record another session consumed mid-run.

phases.description: Ordered navigations sharing one browser context and one carried-state bag. Phases never reorder and an action never splits across contexts.

cleanup_steps.description: Action-scoped finally: runs after the LAST phase regardless of which phase failed, so teardown still happens when a middle phase dies. Gated exactly like mutating steps.

cleanup_path.description: Where cleanup_steps run. Defaults to the LAST phase's resolved path (where the mutation happened). Cleanup opens its own page so a dead phase cannot block teardown — and that page must be navigated somewhere real, because steps on a blank page match no selector and would report a clean teardown that never happened. Supports {{carry.*}}.

require_evidence.description: Action-level evidence requirements, unioned into every phase.

budget_ms.description: Default readiness budget inherited by phases that do not set their own.

noise_patterns.description: Inheritable default for phases; unioned rather than overridden.

viewports.description: Subset of declared viewport names. NOTE: a MUTATING action is pinned to a single viewport regardless — the case expander is a cartesian product, so an unpinned mutating action would execute its mutation once per viewport. The remaining viewports are recorded NOT_TESTED with a reason.

note.description: Annotation only: why this action exists.

action.description: One user-observable action, folded to a single verdict. See definitions.phase for inheritance and the fold rules in walk_verdict.actionVerdict.

type.description: Predicate kind. Every kind compiles to an EXISTING runtime primitive — record_exists/sql to a SELECT-only execute_sql_query with expect/expect_min, feature_enabled/account_can/eval to a project_eval probe with expect. This is a typed facade, not a new checking engine. sql and eval are the escape hatches, so an unanticipated precondition never waits on a schema change.

name.description: Stable id in the report and in precondition_lost accounting.

of.description: record_exists: the table or resource to count.

where.description: record_exists: equality filters, compiled to a parameterized WHERE — never string-interpolated.

permission.description: account_can: the permission the logged-in account must hold.

query.description: sql: SELECT-only. Drivers must reject non-SELECT and cap rows, exactly as runtime.sql does.

eval.description: eval: small read-only Elixir expression for project_eval.

prereq.description: One action precondition. Requires Tidewave: a predicate that cannot be EVALUATED is missing evidence (require_evidence: ["prereq"]) and BLOCKS — it must never degrade to skipped.

from.description: Where to read the value: the landed URL, a selector's text, or a selector's attribute. Deliberately three sources — enough to capture the id of the thing just created, small enough to stay auditable.

pattern.description: from:"url" — regex with exactly one capture group.

required.description: When true (default), a capture that yields nothing BLOCKS the action — a later phase templating {{carry.x}} into a path would otherwise navigate to a literal, land somewhere unintended, and report a confident wrong answer.

as.description: Coercion applied to both sides before comparison.

unit.description: Required unit. Units must match exactly — 1 lb vs 1 kg is a difference even when the number agrees.

normalize.description: Opt-in comparison normalization; literal comparison remains the default. Deliberately a shared definition rather than assert_value-private: this encodes the parity bar (units, displayed precision, currency placement) once, so a future envelope differ consumes the same module instead of reimplementing it.

page.description: A v1 top-level page: one navigation with its own verdict. `name` is required because it keys runtime.per_page and labels the report.

phase.description: One navigation inside an action. Identical to a page except `name` is optional (it defaults to "<action.name> · <ordinal>") and inheritable keys resolve upward: phase → action → walk → driver default. Scalars override; require_evidence and noise_patterns union; runtime deep-merges.

name.description: Stable label used in the report and as key for runtime.per_page.

lands_on.description: Expected landed path (defaults to path). Anti false-green for auth redirects.

budget_ms.description: Readiness budget for navigation plus settle. Assertions and evidence collection are timed separately.

role_gated.description: Annotation only: page requires elevated role.

note.description: Annotation only: why this page is in the walk.

runtime.description: Optional per-page Tidewave/SQL probes (merged over runtime.per_page[name]).

steps.description: Ordered interactions/assertions after navigate+settle. Read-only actions always run; click/fill/type/press require safety.allow_interactions and non-prod env_check.

cleanup_steps.description: Finally-style steps run AFTER the page's steps, screenshot and evidence capture, regardless of the page's outcome — put fixture teardown here. Gated exactly like mutating steps (safety.allow_interactions + non-prod env_check). A cleanup step that fails turns the page ASSERT_FAILED; require_evidence: ["cleanup"] additionally BLOCKS the page when cleanup did not run at all. A page whose steps or cleanup_steps contain mutating actions is pinned to one attempt and never retried.

asset.description: Repo-relative path (e.g. docs/assets/foo.png) that this page's screenshot is published to by product tooling. Only published for a page that PASSed.

viewports.description: Subset of top-level viewport names for this page. Omit to walk every declared viewport.

require_evidence.description: Per-page (per-phase) evidence requirements, merged as a union with the action-level and walk-level lists.

carry.description: Phase-scoped exports into the action's carried-state bag, consumed by later phases as {{carry.<key>}} in path, lands_on and step text. This is what makes "reopen the record I just created" expressible: capture the id here, template it into the next phase's path. Ignored on a v1 top-level page (no action scope to carry into).

mutates.description: Escalate-only override. Mutation is INFERRED from steps/cleanup_steps and that inference is authoritative: a phase containing click/fill/type/... is mutating whether or not this says so, and `false` is NOT honored. Set true for a phase whose navigation alone mutates (e.g. a GET that fires a job), so retry pinning, viewport pinning and the MUTATED_UNVERIFIED fold treat it correctly.

action.description: Step kind. assert_*/wait_for/settle/assert_iframe/assert_http are always allowed; click/fill/type/press/select/check/uncheck/hover are mutating. assert_value reads a form control's VALUE (input/select/textarea) — assert_text cannot see it, because it matches body.innerText and an input's value contributes nothing to innerText. Without assert_value a persistence check is unexpressible.

selector.description: CSS selector (wait_for, assert_selector, click, fill, assert_iframe, …).

frame.description: Scope assert_selector/assert_text/wait_for into an iframe. true = first iframe; or a CSS selector.

iframe.description: Alias for frame (and default selector for assert_iframe).

text.description: Text to assert, fill, or type. For assert_iframe, required content inside the frame.

value.description: Alias for fill/select value, and the expected value for assert_value.

contains.description: assert_value: substring match instead of equality. Mutually exclusive with text/value.

path.description: Expected path fragment for assert_url, or URL path for assert_http.

url.description: Alias for assert_http path (absolute or app-relative).

min_html.description: assert_iframe: minimum HTML length if body text is short (default 800).

url_includes.description: assert_iframe: frame URL must include this substring.

expect_text.description: assert_http: response body must include this.

state.description: wait_for / assert_selector visibility state. "absent" asserts the selector matches NOTHING in the DOM — distinct from "hidden" (present but not visible). assert_selector throws when a selector is missing, so absence was previously unassertable, which blocked permission-negative checks ("this control must NOT exist for a limited account").

event.description: Optional phx-click / event name for deny_events matching.

required.description: When false, a blocked mutating step is SKIPPED instead of FAIL.

continue_on_fail.description: When true, keep running remaining steps after a failure.

safety.description: Agent/operator policy. Default is read-only navigate+screenshot. Mutating pages[].steps require allow_interactions:true and a non-prod env_check strip.

require_loopback_network.description: When true, any browser HTTP(S)/WebSocket request to a non-loopback host is an actionable network failure.

read_only.description: When true (default), mutating steps are blocked unless allow_interactions is also true. Prefer keeping this true and only opting interactions in deliberately.

allow_interactions.description: Opt-in for pages[].steps that click/fill/type/press. Still blocked when env_check finds prod_like values, and still respects deny_events.

env_check.description: Env keys whose values should be inspected for prod write risk (e.g. APP_API_URL). Report surfaces results; mutating steps fail closed if any are prod_like.

deny_events.description: phx-click / event names the walk must never fire (matched against step.event).

runtime.description: Server-side evidence via Tidewave (and optional SQL). When Tidewave is unreachable, the walk still runs; runtime evidence MUST be reported as skipped: tidewave_unavailable.

tidewave.description: When true, collect Tidewave evidence (logs + optional probes). Dev/preview-env only — never prod.

log_levels.description: Server log levels to pull after each page (priority: error, then warning).

probes.description: Allowlisted project_eval checks (walk-level). No free-form eval during a smoke walk.

liveview.description: Default LiveView state capture policy for every page when Tidewave is on.

per_page.description: Map of page name → extra probes/SQL/LiveView for that screen.

require_tidewave.description: When true, fail the whole walk if Tidewave is unavailable (default: skip runtime evidence).

required_tools.description: Exact Tidewave tools that must be present in addition to tools inferred from configured collectors.

default_budget_ms.description: Default readiness budget used when a page has no budget_ms.

fail_on_slow.description: When true, a page that lands correctly after its readiness budget receives hard-failing SLOW instead of PASS_SLOW.

sql.description: SELECT-only probe. Drivers must reject non-SELECT and cap rows. Supports {{carry.*}}.

db_before_after.description: Run a SELECT before navigation and again after the phase's steps, then compare. The window deliberately SPANS navigation, so expect_change:false also catches a plain GET that writes — something the interactions gate cannot see, because no mutating step ever runs. Only digests of the two results are recorded, never rows. Requires Tidewave; a snapshot that could not be taken yields no evidence and BLOCKS under require_evidence.

oneOf.description: Shorthand: the SELECT to compare, recorded without an expectation.

sql.description: SELECT-only. Scope it to the record under test with {{carry.*}} — an unscoped count over a shared dataset reports another session's writes as this action's delta.

expect_change.description: true: this phase MUST have changed the result (proves the write reached the store, not just that the UI said so). false: it must NOT have — the read-only proof, and the higher-value direction, because it turns safety.read_only from a claim into something the run verifies. Omit to record the delta without asserting.

expect_min.description: Minimum numeric result for sql (e.g. count(*)).

expect.description: Exact expected value for a single-cell sql or probe result.

name.description: Stable probe id in the report (e.g. superadmin_role).

eval.description: Small Elixir expression for Tidewave project_eval. Keep pure/read-only; no mutations.

expect.description: If set, probe PASS requires stringified result equality (or boolean/number match).

liveview_probe.description: Capture LiveView process evidence without dumping PII-heavy full assigns into the artifact.

assign_keys.description: Record assign key names only (not values) for hydration proof.

fields.description: Optional small derived facts (e.g. current_user.role) — keep non-PII.

baseline.description: Legacy placeholder; superseded by the top-level visual_baseline config + require_evidence: ["visual_baseline"]. Ignored by drivers.

name.description: Stable label used in the report and screenshot filenames (e.g. mobile, tablet, desktop).

device_scale_factor.description: Defaults to 1. Keep at 1 unless a page is being captured for DPR-sensitive visual diffing — screenshot pixels and DOM bounds only align at DPR 1.

max_attempts.description: Attempts per page (1 = no retry, the v1 default).

retry_on.description: Diagnostic statuses eligible for a retry. The driver honors ONLY TIMEOUT and RUNTIME_ERROR — anything else listed here is dropped and recorded as dropped, never retried: replaying ASSERT_FAILED hides defects, BOUNCED hides access regressions, BLOCKED hides missing evidence. Pages with mutating steps never retry regardless.

record_flakiness.description: When true the report records attempts, per-attempt statuses, and marks a page FLAKY when attempts disagree. A flaky page still reports its final class.
